full_judgment:
4. The case for the defence is that the accused-appellant neither promised to marry P.W. 1 Begum Akhtar Khatun nor had any sexual intercourse with her. She used to mix with several persons including her sister's husband, cousins, boyfriends, servants, etc. She used to sometimes live in the house of her sister's husband Altu. She also used to occasionally live in the house of her maternal uncle Jahed Ali who had two sons and three or four servants with whom she used to mix. She became pregnant by having sexual intercourse with some other persons. She also worked as maid-servant in some houses and also used to gossip with Mati and Kuchan who are neighbours of her brother-in-law Altu. There is a boundary dispute between Jahed Ali; the maternal uncle of prosecutrix P.W.1 Begum Akhtar Khatun and Latif, the father of accused-appellant Abed Ali. In the civil suit between them appellant's father Latif got the decree against complainant's maternal uncle Jahed Ali. It is her maternal uncle Jahed Ali who took P.W. 1 Begum. Akhtar Khatun to the Court and got a false complaint written and lodged against the accused out of grudge. The story of holding of any salish is also false and concocted. The accused appellant has been falsely implicated in this case. 

 14. None of the prosecution witnesses stated that accused appellant Abed Ali by deceit caused P. W. 1 Begum Akhtar Khatun to believe that she was lawfully married to accused appellant Abed Ali. On the contrary P. W. 9 Sabuj Mia admitted that there was enmity over the lands between P. W. 4 Hira Miah, uncle of P. W. 1 and father of accused appellant Abed Ali and that neither before nor after the lodging of the present case P. W. 1 Begum Akhter Khatun gave out that accused-appellant Abed Ali had sexual intercourse with her or was responsible for making her pregnant P. W. 5 admitted that P.W. 1. used to work in different houses. P.W. 1 Begum Akhtar Khatun herself admitted that the house of accused appellant Abed Ali is situated to the adjacent north of the house of her maternal uncle Jahed Ali, that there is boundary dispute and litigation between her maternal uncle Jahed Ali and Latif,  father of accused-appellant Abed Ali, that appellant's father Latif obtained a decree against her maternal uncle Jahed Ali, that occasionally she lived in the house of her maternal uncle Jahed Ali who had two sons and three or four servants with whom she used to mix and talk and that it was her maternal uncle Jahed Ali who got the petition of complaint Ext. 1 drafted (by the advocate P.W. 6 Abdul Jahed Ahmed). She also admitted that accused Abed Ali's father Latif got decree against her maternal uncle Jahed Ali. She also stated that sometimes she used to live at the house of her sister's husband Altu and that she used to mix and gossip with two young men, namely, Mati and Kuchan who are neighbors of her brother-in-law Altu.
